Subject: Hosted API pricing — custom throughput bands?

Hi Neha,

We're running a model migration at FastRetail and trying to build a cost model for next quarter. Our expected token volume is spiky — baseline ~250M tokens/day with holiday peaks up to ~1.1B/day for ~48 hours. HubSpot record is linked below.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide an indicative hosted API rate card that includes a custom band for sustained 250–500M/day and a higher band for burst windows (500M–1.2B/day)?
2) How do committed discounts interact with burst overage — do you allow temporary burst credits or rollover?

I've attached a simple throughput model (FastRetail_throughput_model.xlsx). We're aiming to finalize procurement sizing with finance by 02/20.

Appreciate any pointers — would love a short call if that helps.

Thanks,

Hi Sophie — thanks for the model, this is helpful. Looping in Ben (pricing) and Laura (AE) to propose structures. A few quick clarifying Qs before we draft a short options matrix: 

- Is the 250M/day baseline expected to be sustained every weekday (M–F) or averaged across a 7-day window?
- For the 48-hour holiday spike, do you want guaranteed headroom (reserved capacity) or best-effort burst on hosted?
- Any internal procurement constraints on contract length (12/24/36 months) that would affect discount bands?

We can share a PDF of our hosted API rate card as a starting point and then sketch two tailored proposals: 1) committed slab (discounts applied to committed monthly tokens + overage rates), and 2) committed + burst credits (pre-purchased burst pool that can be consumed without overage penalties).

Hi Sophie / team — attaching our Hosted API ratecard (Redwood_Hosted_Ratecard_v2.pdf) and a short worked example based on the XLS you sent. High level: 

Option A — Committed Slab (12 mo):
- Commit: 6.5B tokens/month (~216M/day). 18% discount off list for generation tokens, 12% for embeddings.
- Overage: 30% premium over list for sustained overruns >10% of committed in a billing month.

Option B — Commit + Burst Pool (12–24 mo):
- Commit: 5B tokens/month. Add burst pool (1.5B tokens/month) pre-purchased at 10% discount vs list. Burst pool is consumed first during spikes; unused pool does not roll over.

Option C — Reserved Capacity Add-on (Dedicated-like headroom for holidays):
- Short-term reserved instances for 48–72 hour windows priced as an hourly block (quoted separately per region).

Notes:
- We can tier discounts by commit length (12/24/36 mo) and by smoothing (if you commit to smoothing windows we can reduce overage penalties).
- For multi-day spikes we recommend the burst pool or short-term reserved capacity — hosted best-effort can handle <2x sustained for short windows but we don’t guarantee capacity without reservation.

Attaching examples: worked_calculation_fastretail.pdf (inline in ratecard). Let us know which option you prefer and we’ll put numbers into a mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

3) Reserved holiday headroom: pricing for 48–72 hour reserved blocks will be quoted post-call (region-dependent).
